lesson_intent.one_sentence_goal: Practice måste plus infinitive for simple needs and obligations.
lesson_intent.real_life_context: A colleague explains errands and time pressure after work.
lesson_intent.communicative_function: Saying what someone has to do and responding politely.

dialogue_task.scenario: Anna and Erik talk before leaving work. One has to shop, call someone, or go to a meeting, and the other responds with understanding.

main_focus.name: måste plus infinitive
main_focus.description: Use måste before an infinitive to express a necessary action.
main_focus.desired_presence: Use måste plus infinitive naturally 4-5 times in the dialogue.

vocabulary_target.desired_presence: Use everyday obligations, not heavy work-specific tasks.

dialogue_shape.opening: One speaker asks if the other can stay or take fika.
dialogue_shape.middle: The other explains one or two things they have to do, with a short response from the colleague.
dialogue_shape.ending: They end politely and agree to talk later.

target_complexity.repetition: repeat måste in statements and one question

focus: what one speaker has to do
why the speaker cannot stay long
how the other speaker responds politely

sentence_focus: one sentence about shopping after work
one sentence about not having time
